SMTO-EXE-0259 — This workflow needs a value that wasn't provided

GUID: 2a05ad30-2176-575a-9731-0e02e417e310
Slug: recipe-parameter-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • This workflow has a required input, such as a file name or address, that has no value for this run. SMTO stopped before running any of the workflow's steps.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation where this workflow came from and find your original request. That request shows what the workflow is meant to do and which value it needs.
  2. Select Save to workflow on that message, write the missing value, such as the file name, directly into the request, then select Save workflow. Workflows saved this way keep the full request, so they don't need separate values.
  3. If the value is private, such as a password, type @ and the Parameter Store entry's name instead of the value itself. SMTO won't save passwords inside a workflow, but it can look them up when it runs.
  4. Run the new workflow from Workflows with Run now, and remove any schedule that still uses the old one. The old workflow will keep stopping here because it still has no value.

What success looks like

  • The new workflow starts and its task runs without asking for a missing value.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO; they can see which value the older workflow expects.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recorded-workflow parameter validation found a required declared parameter with no supplied or default value, or a step referenced a parameter missing from the invocation values.

What this means

  • A required declared parameter has no supplied/default value, or rendering references a parameter absent from the invocation values. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A required declared parameter has no supplied/default value, or rendering references a parameter absent from the invocation values.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the missing parameter name and its schema, default and required flag without exposing private values.

How to fix it

  • Compare the recipe's parameter_schema and default_parameters with the invocation's agent_recipe_parameter_values (validation.parameters, bindings.render). Supply the value or a default through the API or schedule that starts the recorded workflow, or re-save it as a saved-request workflow, which has no parameters.
  • Supply the missing value through the workflow parameter form, using a reference where the parameter requires one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • All required parameters resolve and satisfy the workflow's parameter validation.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
